title: Ecosystem, certifications, and the UC bridge
summary: Name only the certifications this edition confirmed, and keep CUCM, UCCX, CVP, and Webex Calling in their real roles.

lessons.title: A glossary tied to a document
lessons.summary: Every term in your notes points at a role and a document, not at a product logo.
objectives: Write the expansion and the role
Attach a cite key that exists
Keep product names out of the role column

illustration.title: A row in the glossary
illustration.caption: If you cannot name the document, the row is not ready.

paragraphs: When you meet a term, write the expansion, the role it plays on a ladder, and the document that defines it. SIP, SDP, and RTP stay three rows. An SBC is usually a B2BUA in the sense RFC 7092 taxonomizes, which is a different row from a pure proxy.

Product names go in a separate column. CUCM can hold registrar and call-control duties. CUBE is a B2BUA you configure from the CUBE basic guide. The glossary row still says the role. The logo does not become the definition.

A row without a document waits. This library's cite keys are the allowed pointers. If a neighbor system has no SIP RFC, the row says so, and you cite the vendor series page or you leave the protocol column blank on purpose.
Re-read the row the next time the RFC Editor header moves. SDP's row in this edition says RFC 8866, with RFC 4566 named as the document it moved from. The header is how you update the row later.

quiz.q: A glossary row contains
choices: The term, the role, and the document
quiz.why: The document is a cite key or an honest gap.

quiz.q: An SBC's usual role name is
quiz.why: RFC 7092 is the taxonomy. The product guide is a separate column.

quiz.q: CUCM in the glossary is
choices: A product that can be the registrar and the call-control point
The definition of a proxy in RFC 3261
quiz.why: Cite cucm for the product and RFC 3261 for the role.

quiz.q: SDP's row in this edition cites
quiz.why: RFC 4566 is the predecessor you mention, not the current number.

quiz.q: A neighbor with no SIP RFC
choices: Gets an honest gap, not a fake RFC number
quiz.why: Say there is no SIP RFC in this library. Cite a vendor page when you have one.

quiz.q: The 2xx ACK row cites
quiz.why: End-to-end ACK is a protocol fact, not a product feature.

cards.back: What the box does on the ladder: UA, proxy, registrar, B2BUA.
UAS plus UAC. RFC 7092. Typical SBC.
The cite you can open. A logo is not a document.
RFC 8866 now. RFC 4566 is the one it moved from.

steps: Press Play.

check.q: The glossary role for a typical SBC is
check.why: RFC 7092. The product name stays in the other column.

fault.title: Logo in the role column
fault.symptom: A ticket says the failed hop is a CUCM, so the status code must be a CUCM invention. The message is SIP/2.0 180 Ringing with a normal To tag.
fault.log:
SIP/2.0 180 Ringing
Call-ID: a84b4c76e66710@example.com
CSeq: 1 INVITE
Ticket role: CUCM (no RFC cited)
choices: Call 180 Ringing a SIP provisional, and name CUCM as the product
Replace the glossary with the logo only
Cite a fake RFC for the product name
fault.why: 180 is RFC 3261 section 21. CUCM is the product series that sent or forwarded it.
fault.cause: The role column and the product column were the same cell.
fault.fix: Write UA or B2BUA or proxy for the role, cite RFC 3261, and put CUCM in the product column with its series page.

lessons.title: Neighbors that are not SIP elements
lessons.summary: WFM and QM are operations systems. CRM is not a SIP element. Recording, location, and the media path keep their real documents.
objectives: Place WFM and QM outside the SIP RFC set
Tie recording to SIPREC and emergency to the BCP
Leave CRM off the ladder

illustration.title: Who sits where
illustration.caption: SIP still carries the session. Several neighbors never appear as a Via.

layers.name: SIPREC / emergency
layers.detail: RFC 7866 and RFC 6881 when those features are on

layers.name: WFM, QM, CRM
layers.detail: Operations or business systems. No SIP RFC invented here.

paragraphs: Workforce management and quality management are contact-center operations systems. This library has no SIP RFC for them, and this lesson does not invent one. They consume events and recordings from the contact center. They do not appear as the Via that routed the INVITE.

Recording that the SBC forks is SIPREC. Cite RFC 7866 for the protocol and RFC 7865 for metadata. That is the SIP-adjacent neighbor. Quality management may listen to the result. The listening product is not itself RFC 7866.

sections.h: Location, analytics, and the media path
paragraphs: Emergency calling stays with RFC 6881, RFC 6442, and the FCC MLTS page. Analytics and AI agents sit above the media path. SIP still carries the session. RTP still carries the voice once the answer is done. An insight attached to a Call-ID is not a new SIP method.

CRM is not a SIP element. This lesson does not invent product features for Salesforce or any other CRM. A screen pop may use a Call-ID your contact center already has. The CRM does not authenticate the INVITE, choose the codec, or terminate the carrier trunk.
Unity Connection is a messaging application reached through the call-control platform. It is not the PSTN trunk point. Cite its series page for the product, and keep the trunk on CUBE or CUCM.
When a neighbor has a series page in this library, use that page. When it does not, say the gap. WFM and QM are in the gap on purpose.

quiz.q: WFM and QM in this lesson are
choices: Contact-center operations systems, with no SIP RFC invented for them
quiz.why: Say the gap. Do not coin an RFC number.

quiz.q: A disclosed SBC recording cites
quiz.why: SIPREC is the SIP neighbor. QM may use the recording afterward.

quiz.q: CRM is
quiz.why: No Salesforce feature list belongs in this lesson.

quiz.q: Analytics and AI agents
choices: Sit above the media path while SIP carries the session
quiz.why: RTP still carries voice. The agent is not a SIP role.

quiz.q: Emergency location stays with
choices: RFC 6881, RFC 6442, and the FCC MLTS page
The CRM object's custom fields only
quiz.why: National rules point at the FCC page. State PSAP rules are not invented here.

quiz.q: Unity Connection is
choices: A messaging application, not the PSTN trunk point
quiz.why: Trunks land on CUBE or CUCM. Cite the Unity series page for messaging.

cards.back: Operations systems. No SIP RFC in this library.
The recording neighbor that is SIP. RFC 7866 and RFC 7865.
Not a SIP element. No invented vendor features.
Analytics and agents. SIP and RTP still carry the session.

fault.title: A CRM field treated as Geolocation
fault.symptom: An emergency INVITE copies a CRM city string into a private header and omits RFC 6442 location. The ticket calls the private header sufficient for RAY BAUM's Act.
fault.log:
INVITE urn:service:sos SIP/2.0
X-Crm-City: example
Call-ID: sos-1@example.com
(no Geolocation)
choices: Carry location per RFC 6442 and check the FCC MLTS page
The CRM city string is the conveyance specification
fault.why: CRM is not a SIP location element. RFC 6442 is the conveyance specification.
fault.cause: A business-system field was substituted for the emergency documents.
fault.fix: Send location as RFC 6442 describes, keep the service URN, and confirm Kari's Law and RAY BAUM's Act on the FCC page.

lessons.title: Workforce tools and agents above the media
lessons.summary: Agents and workforce tools sit above the media path. The session is still SIP, and the voice is still RTP.
objectives: Keep SIP as the session protocol
Place AI assistance above RTP
Refuse invented agent features

illustration.title: Stack, from the wire up
illustration.caption: Assistance that cannot see SIP still does not become SIP.

layers.name: Assist
layers.detail: WFM, QM, analytics, agents. Above the media path.

sections.h: The session does not move upstairs
paragraphs: An agent that summarizes a call, suggests a reply, or scores a conversation is using the contact center's own application interfaces. The SIP dialog is still between the user agents and the B2BUA. Call-ID, CSeq, and the To tag still identify that dialog.

RTP, RFC 3550, still carries the samples. If the assistant needs the words, something in the disclosed recording or the contact-center media path provided them. This lesson does not describe a hidden tap. Disclosed recording stays SIPREC when the SBC forks to an SRS.

This edition does not invent features for a named AI product, a named CRM, or a named workforce suite. If a design needs one of those, cite that vendor's current guide, which may not be in this library. Say the gap.

Workforce schedules and quality scores can change how many people are on shift. They do not change 180 into 200, and they do not select the codec. When the ladder is wrong, fix the ladder. When the schedule is wrong, fix the schedule in its own system.

paragraphs: SIP School Certified Associate is SSCA Elite. Cite the SSCA page and the SIP School courses page. The courses page also lists SSVVP and SSSP. This lesson does not expand those two acronyms. The courses page is the label.
The SSCA page says passing is worth 20 CEC credits toward a BICSI certification. That sentence is cited to the SSCA page. If the page changes the credit number, the page wins.

CCNP Collaboration is the core exam 350-801 CLCOR plus one concentration: 300-815 CLACC, 300-820 CLHCT, or 300-830 CLCCE. CLCOR also earns Cisco Certified Specialist - Collaboration Core. CCIE Collaboration is the core exam plus the lab exam. Cite the CCNP page, the CLCOR page, the Cisco exams list, and the learning-network update page.

The learning-network update page says the first date to test for the Collaboration Cloud Customer Experience specialist was February 3, 2026. This lesson invents no other dates. Exam topics change, and the Cisco page wins.

sections.h: Microsoft, and the codes this edition will not invent
paragraphs: Microsoft 365 Certified: Collaboration Communications Systems Engineer Associate is exam MS-721. Cite the certification page and the study guide. For a Cisco credential, open the CCNP page, the CLCOR page, and the exams list. The learning-network update page is where this edition read February 3, 2026 as the first test date for the Collaboration Cloud Customer Experience specialist. Exam topics change, and the Cisco page wins. For Microsoft, open the MS-721 certification page and the study guide.

Other dates are not in this lesson.
A blog that disagrees with the RFC Editor banner loses. A blog that disagrees with the Cisco or Microsoft page loses. Write the URL you opened, which in this curriculum is the cite key, and move on.

layers.name: UCCX / CVP
layers.detail: Contact center through CUCM, or SIP as that version's CVP guide describes

paragraphs: CUCM is the call-control registrar and trunk point in this picture. Phones register there. Trunks toward CUBE or a carrier are configured there. Cite the CUCM series page for the product, and cite RFC 3261 for the SIP those trunks speak.

CUBE, when it is the border, is the B2BUA that faces the carrier. The basic CUBE SIP guide is the configuration context. The carrier INVITE in this lab arrives at 203.0.113.20 from 192.0.2.40, and CUCM at 198.51.100.30 is the call agent behind it.
UCCX call control is through CUCM. The product series page is uccx. This lesson does not claim that UCCX terminates carrier SIP trunks. PSTN SIP lands on CUBE or CUCM.
Agent legs, route points, and queue treatment are CUCM's call-control relationship with UCCX. Drawing the carrier INVITE as if it ended on UCCX is the picture this lesson refuses.

sections.h: CVP, by the guide you actually have
paragraphs: CVP configuration guides describe SIP between CVP, gateways, and CUCM. Cite the CVP series page, then open the guide for the exact version you run. The version decides the call flow. This lesson does not invent a comprehensive script.

If you need a sequence for a design review, copy it from that version's guide and label the version. A remembered comprehensive flow from a different release is how trunks get drawn onto the wrong box.

lessons.title: Webex Calling local gateway, and a separate contact center
lessons.summary: Premises PSTN for Webex Calling uses Local Gateway. Webex Contact Center is a separate product with its own design guide.
objectives: Place premises PSTN on the Local Gateway pattern
Cite the Webex Calling PSTN and Local Gateway pages
Keep Webex Contact Center off this pattern until its own guide says otherwise

illustration.caption: The edge hostname in production comes from the Local Gateway guide. This ladder uses example.com so it does not invent that name.

layers.name: Webex Calling
layers.detail: Cloud call control. Not the contact-center product.

paragraphs: Webex Calling premises PSTN uses a local gateway. Cite the get-started Local Gateway page and the page that configures Webex Calling PSTN for the organization. The gateway in this lab is the border address 203.0.113.20, and the carrier is 192.0.2.40.

The production Request-URI and the Webex edge hostname come from the Local Gateway guide for the tenant you are building. The synthetic INVITE uses example.com so this lesson does not invent that hostname. Read the guide before you copy a target into a trunk.

Webex Contact Center is a separate product. This lesson does not claim it uses the same Local Gateway pattern. Check Cisco's current Webex Contact Center design guide before you reuse this picture. This library has no cite key for that guide, so the lesson names the document and does not invent a URL.

Call control in the Webex Calling picture is the Webex Calling organization, reached through the local gateway. CUCM-style trunks from the previous lesson are a different bridge. Say which product you are in before you draw the arrow.
